newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to become freight integrator.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to become freight integrator.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG will be developed from a simple freight airline to a global logistics supplier operating as an integrator for standard freight, Deutsche Lufthansa chairman Juergen Weber told a freight managers congress.

The autonomous Lufthansa freight subsidiary aims to become the leading logistics services provider in the global air cargo industry within the next 10 years, Weber said in a speech to the annual congress of the German shippers association (BVL).
Lufthansa Cargo needs to develop its activities in line with a general economic globalisation as corporate purchasing, production and sales markets spread across the world, he said.

"In a global company I see in this move into logistics systems the appropriate role for a highly developed transport company like Lufthansa Cargo," he told the 1,400 corporate logistics managers and other congress delegates.
"Transport as a commodity will certainly remain and we will play our role in it, but the main thrust will be in modern logistics systems," he added.
Lufthansa Cargo, a 100 percent subsidiary since January 1955, would function as a kind of "standard freight intergrator" together with selected partners, he said.
"We do not want to do this alone but in a group system for distribution, logistics and transport to ensure a smooth path from the shipper to the receiving customer," he said.

Companies seeking to link production locations in Europe and Asia did not want to work with 20 airlines, 70 freight forwarders and dozens of other service providers, but sought as few transport partners as possible, he said.
Lufthansa Cargo would expand airport-to-airport services to "modular" door-to-door services in co-operation with partners such as DHL International.
"Regarding delivery times, quality and availability we will develop them into a unique range services with short and guaranteed delivery times to all points of the globe," Weber said.
Lufthansa Cargo had already developed a worldwide network of freight hubs such as Sharjah, Miami, and Moscow based on Frankfurt as the central point, he added.

Lufthansa Cargo is currently the largest international cargo airline with a world market share of about nine perecent but is running at a loss in 1966, industry observers noted. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
